clue.text: Studies on sleep?

parts.note: crash is slang for sleep and courses are programmes of study, so studies on sleep reads as a pun on intensive short training

explanation.surface: An academic programme about how and why we sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests research into sleep, but 'crash' means to fall asleep, and the phrase is really a short burst of intensive study.
explanation.definitionFit: A cram course compresses a subject into intensive short study, punningly courses that 'crash'.

clue.text: If a sailor set up a drink.

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the words before it are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor knocks back a drink he has prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IF A TAR into RATAFI; the second 'a' then adds the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond-flavoured liqueur, so a kind of drink.

clue.text: … men so dry displayed symptoms

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are spread out and laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Dehydrated men showing signs of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' signals the anagram of MEN SO DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a recognised group of symptoms occurring together.

clue.text: Reduce energy — it's precious!

parts.note: to reduce something is to cut it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that cutting back on energy is a valuable thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' here means twee or affectedly sweet, not valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious in the sense of overly sweet or twee is a synonym of cute.

clue.text: The sort of bread to lend a venue style

indicators.note: to style something is to shape or arrange it, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Giving a venue some style, it seems, is like a kind of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is used as a verb signalling the anagram of LEND A VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleavened bread is made without yeast or raising agent, a recognised variety.

clue.text: Total oil deposit outside Uruguay

indicators.note: outside says the first piece sits around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a sump is the reservoir of oil at the bottom of an engine
U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay

explanation.surface: Adding up the oil reserves found beyond Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total' is a verb here: to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to add them together into a single sum.

clue.text: Has spin developed into language?

indicators.note: developed into suggests the letters have grown into a fresh form, a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether some political spin has turned into its own way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed into' signals the anagram of HAS SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish is the language of Spain and much of Latin America.

clue.text: Purchases that add spice to journeys

definitions.text: Purchases that add spice to journeys

parts.words: Purchases that add spice to journeys
parts.note: to season is to add spice, so a playful reading of travel passes bought for a whole period as things that flavour trips

explanation.surface: Buying something to make travelling more exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' is read as a cooking verb, though here it means a period of time for which a pass is valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Commuters buy passes covering a whole period of travel, punningly seasoning their journeys.

clue.text: Should one cast lots?

parts.note: casting lots is drawing to decide by chance, but here the question hints at someone who foretells many fates or casts them

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone should draw lots to decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' means fates or fortunes, which a seer may 'cast' as a horoscope is cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant predicts people's futures, reading out their lots in life.

clue.text: Former money court that is no longer!

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: An old currency court that has since been abolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct has died out and no longer exists.

clue.text: Left university doctor with a good old back problem

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor leaving the university with a long-standing bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: A string of abbreviations; MB is the British medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles and joints of the lower spine.

clue.text: Settle with revolutionary leader -until now!

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench with a high back, a kind of seat like a sofa

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Settling matters with a revolutionary leader so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' looks like a verb but is the noun for a high-backed bench.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is an idiom meaning up to the present time.

clue.text: Make up or bend out of shape a tin?

parts.note: to warp is to bend or twist

indicators.note: out of shape says the following letters lose their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether to apply cosmetics or to bend a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' signals the anagram of A TIN, giving AINT.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is facetious slang for cosmetics, a woman's make-up.

clue.text: When like this, spies put up companions

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
so means in this way
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set something is to put it

explanation.surface: Spies setting up their associates in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Associates are partners or companions in some activity.

clue.text: Fails to follow approach, causing collisions, almost

indicators.note: to follow says the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: to near something is to approach it
misses means fails to hit

explanation.surface: Drivers failing to keep distance and almost crashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a narrowly avoided collision.

clue.text: Almost consider being slim!

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, dropping its final letter

parts.note: to think is to consider

explanation.surface: Thinking about becoming slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and slim are synonyms describing a slender build.

clue.text: List spam sent to songwriter

indicators.note: sent suggests the letters are sent off in confusion, scrambled

explanation.surface: Junk email being forwarded to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' signals the anagram of LIST SPAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist writes psalms, sacred songs, King David being the archetype.

clue.text: Very keen on it, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A question about being enthusiastic about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very keen on it' looks like one phrase, but 'on it' is anagram fodder with 'perhaps' as indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is an informal idiom for being very enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: They offer digital coverage

parts.note: digital means relating to fingers and toes, so this coverage protects digits, not a TV signal

explanation.surface: Broadcasters offering digital television services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests broadcasting, but digits include toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toecaps are reinforced coverings over the front of boots that protect the toes.

clue.text: During which heads are almost sure to roll?

definitions.text: During which heads are almost sure to roll?

parts.words: During which heads are almost sure to roll?
parts.note: heads rolling usually means sackings, but here a gymnast's head literally rolls over during a flip

explanation.surface: A purge in which people will almost certainly be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads roll' is an idiom for dismissals, but here it is a literal tumble head over heels.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flip head over heels the body rotates and the head turns through a full circle.

clue.text: Nuclear explosion not easily explained

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A nuclear blast whose cause is obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' signals the anagram of NUCLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear means obscure or hard to understand.

clue.text: Persist and financially support a bird

parts.note: to keep someone is to provide for them financially
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Persevering in paying for a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep at it is an idiom urging someone to persevere.

clue.text: When TV is something worth having?

parts.note: as can mean when
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A question of when a television is valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: Anaesthetic found in public house

definitions.meaning: an anaesthetic numbing only one part of the body
in British usage, the neighbourhood pub one habitually drinks at

explanation.surface: A painkiller turning up in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is both a localised anaesthetic and, in Britain, one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are common British usage: a numbing injection and the nearby pub.

clue.text: Gamble on a letter to the Greeks

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Placing a bet on a letter to Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Managed to pose after time in passage

indicators.note: after says the words before it come after time in the answer

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, past tense ran
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone who has managed to pose for a picture while in transit.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Why things look bad?

parts.note: look bad suggests an unattractive appearance, but here it means a malevolent glance that brings misfortune

explanation.surface: A question about why matters appear bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'look bad' is reread: a harmful look cast at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious stare believed to cause harm or bad luck to its target.

clue.text: A Tory fascist might be okay!

indicators.note: might be suggests these letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a right-wing extremist would be acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' signals the anagram of A TORY FASCIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means acceptable or adequate, much like okay.
